Danish Energy Agency (2024). Technology Data for Carbon Capture, Transport and Storage. Technology descriptions and projections for long-term energy system planning. Version 0003, April 2024 (first published November 2021 by the Danish Energy Agency and Energinet). ISBN 978-87-94447-14-0. https://ens.dk/technologydata. Data sheets: technology_data_for_carbon_capture_transport_storage.xlsx.

All costs are real 2020 EUR excl. VAT (PDF p.11; workbook Index "All cost data is in 2020 EURO"; Index change log 31/8/2023 "Update to 2020 prices"). Rows in sheets 422, 423 and co2 terminals carry no priceyear in alldata_flat and are taken as 2020 EUR per the Index.

Source: alldata_flat sheet, cross-checked against the per-technology sheets, notes and the PDF guideline. Main file: the 2020 central value (first data year). Sheets 401-412, 421 and 451 print lower/upper ONLY for 2025 and 2050, so 2020 rows carry no min/max; the 2025 central with its lower/upper and 2030/2040/2050 go to _projections.csv. Sheets 422, 423 and co2 terminals print 2020 lower/upper, used as min/max. LOADED FULLY - capture (401.a-c, 402.a-b, 403.a-b): capacity (t CO2/h), capex and fixed O&M kept per (t CO2/h) because no operating hours are printed for these (see defects), variable O&M per t CO2, specific energy (heat, electricity) in MWh/t, capture rate, lifetime, construction time; liquefaction 411: capex and fixed O&M converted to per t of annual capacity with the printed 96% up-time (note F), availability, electricity (compression+drying+liquefaction). Electricity for 401.x = capture plant + printed liquefaction electricity (the capex includes compression and liquefaction); 402.a = plant (0) + CPU (ASU excluded, as from the capex); 402.b = CPU + ASU (ASU inside the capex). DAC electricity excludes compression, as the DAC capex does (PDF p.88). Capex cost basis: DEA investment = EPC/overnight incl. equipment and installation (PDF p.13), recorded as installed for DAC and liquefaction and as incremental for the capture retrofits (401, 402). Flows: amine make-up, O2 (402.a), DAC water, recoverable heat outputs (waste-heat). TRANSPORT and STORAGE: lifetime, construction time; storage (451.x) also injection capacity (Mt/yr), power consumption (MJ/t injected, as electricity) and variable O&M excl. energy (EUR/t injected). NOT LOADED (in _other-values.csv): pipeline costs (EUR per (t/h) per metre, per (t/h)/yr/km), truck costs (EUR/t and EUR/t/km), ship and terminal costs (EUR per t of cargo/tank capacity), 412 tank and truck-filling costs, storage capex / fixed O&M / decommissioning / pre-FID / post-closure costs (per t of cumulative injected CO2, not per annual capacity), ASU option costs for 402.a, start-up costs, outages, flue-gas data, CO2 purity and pressure, heat-out temperatures, land use, condensate and component energy rows.

(1) Uncertainty ranges for the capture, liquefaction, intermediate storage, pipeline and storage sheets are printed for 2025 and 2050 only, not for the 2020 first year; the 2020 central often lies outside the 2025 range (e.g. 401.a capex 8.3 vs 2025 range 3.54-8.26), so no min/max is attached to 2020.; (2) Capture capex and fixed O&M are per (t CO2/h) with no technology-specific operating hours; guideline Table 2 (p.22) ties capture operation to the host plant (CHP back-pressure 4000 h, extraction 4000-5000 h, MSW/biogas stand-alone 8000 h) but 401.a (WtE or biomass CHP) and the others do not say which applies, so no per-t-per-yr conversion was made (unit 2020_EUR-million/(t-per-h); fixed O&M 2020_EUR-million/(t-per-h)-yr, printed without an explicit per-year).; (3) 401.a/b note I includes owner's costs in the retrofit capex, contradicting the guideline (p.13-14), which excludes owners' predevelopment costs.; (4) 402.a and 402.b print capture rate, CO2 purity, CO2 and H2O shares and forced outage as fractions in columns labelled %; capture rate converted x100.; (5) 402.b heat out is labelled MW/tCO2 (not MW/(tCO2/h) as in 402.a); left in _other-values.; (6) 403.a: 2020 capacity is 0.045 t/h (Carbon Engineering pilot) while costs come from learning curves for a 1 Mt/y plant (p.88); 2020 heat input (1.23) is printed only for 2020 and electricity jumps from 0.36 (2020) to 1.458 (2025) on assumed full electrification (note E). Fixed O&M note K says it is TOTAL O&M (3.7% of capex) yet a separate variable O&M row is printed.; (7) 403.b fixed O&M is total O&M not split (notes K/L).; (8) 411 note F gives 96% up-time while guideline Table 2 gives 8000 full-load hours for biogas stand-alone plants; the sheet-specific 96% was used. Note B cites 200-225 kWh/t supplier electricity incl. pumping vs 137 kWh/t summed from the rows.; (9) 401.c heat out (1.65 MWh/t) exceeds heat input (0.833 MWh/t, same as the biomass cases) with no explanation beyond flue-gas pre-cooling.; (10) alldata_flat Ref column for 422, 423 and co2 terminals holds numbers 1.912, 2.868, 0.956 that are not reference numbers (multiples of 0.956, apparently a price-index factor); these rows also have no priceyear.; (11) 422 and terminal fixed O&M/cost rows print lower and upper as 0 (placeholders); 423 variable O&M row label reads 14000 t ship with unit EUR/[t CO2/h]/.; (12) 451 storage costs are per t of cumulative injected CO2, and the injected totals used (onshore: 84 Mt for 3 Mt/y, 130 Mt for 5 Mt/y; PDF Table 0-5, p.183-184) differ from the printed storage capacity (90, 150 Mt) that note A defines as injection rate x lifetime; energy is 50 MJ/t in the sheets vs 49 MJ/t in the PDF tables. Offshore energy cost is based on green ammonia (note J) though the row is labelled power consumption.; (13) PDF guideline page footers read "Technology Data for Industrial Process heat and CC" (copied from another catalogue); Table 3 reference is a broken cross-reference ("Fejl! Henvisningskilde ikke fundet").; (14) Typos in sheet names/titles: "Direct air capure", "Oxy-fuel carbon caputre", "Eletricity input".
